title: Felix and the Atlas
premise: In 1746, Gideon Thackeray secretly finishes the Atlas Felix — the masterwork his mentor died protecting — while hiding from the Admiralty men who burned the old cartographer's workshop. When a stranger arrives bearing letters in the master's unmistakable hand, Gideon learns he is alive, imprisoned, and that the atlas itself is the ransom. As evacuation orders fall on the coastal town, Gideon must choose between delivering the atlas to save his master and giving the last berth on the fleeing ship to Felix, the orphan boy the master raised as a son. In the end, Gideon surrenders the atlas to the Admiralty, keeps the boy, and discovers the master smuggled the true maps inside Felix's memory — taught to him as nursery rhymes and star songs all along.
about_author: Ada Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime charts in a coastal museum, where the marginalia of forgotten mapmakers first captured her imagination. She writes historical fiction about the people history records only in footnotes.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Paper
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Three months after Master Aldous Felix's presumed death, Gideon works by candlelight completing the Atlas Felix, hiding pages inside the false bottom of a sea chest. Felix, the master's orphan ward, keeps watch for Admiralty riders. When a stranger named Corvane arrives soaked from the crossing, carrying letters in the master's living hand, Gideon's careful invisibility shatters. Beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope.

chapters.title: Ink and Ransom
chapters.summary: Alternating Gideon and Felix POV. Corvane reveals the master lives in a debtor prison, and the Admiralty will trade his freedom for the atlas — the charts they burned him for. Gideon begins copying the atlas to keep both, while Felix, who suspects he'll be left behind, quietly teaches himself the master's surveying methods to prove his worth. Admiralty scouts reach the harbor. Beat: love curdling into bargaining, each person measuring what they can carry.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, then Gideon's. Evacuation is ordered; the packet ship takes only those with papers. Gideon faces the choice the blurb promises — the atlas can buy the master's release, but the ship's final berth belongs to either the atlas's courier or the boy. Felix, overhearing, offers to stay and vanishes into the press-ganged docks. Gideon finds him at the master's ruined workshop and realizes Felix can redraw every chart from memory. Beat: the climax — Gideon surrenders the atlas to Corvane, betting everything on the boy.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Gideon and Felix's shared POV. Aboard the departing ship, they learn Corvane was the master's son, sent not to ransom but to rescue what mattered: not the atlas, but the apprentice who loved it. The master, freed by the Admiralty's acquisition, chose to stay behind and let the boy go — his last act of fatherhood. On the open water, Felix begins teaching Gideon the star songs. Beat: belonging redefined — family is what survives the crossing.
